title: SMTO-EXE-0138 — SMTO can't read the buttons and fields of apps on that computer
summary: SMTO couldn't read the buttons and text fields of apps on the Gateway's computer, because that computer's accessibility features aren't working for it right now. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0138 — SMTO can't read the buttons and fields of apps on that computer

html:
SMTO-EXE-0138 — SMTO can't read the buttons and fields of apps on that computer

GUID: d29d0899-60c9-5590-8f7d-989d88627519
Slug: ui-accessibility-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't read the buttons and text fields of apps on the Gateway's computer, because that computer's accessibility features aren't working for it right now. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), make sure a user is signed in and the desktop is awake and unlocked. Apps only share their buttons and fields with SMTO inside a signed-in desktop.
  2. Ask whoever manages that computer to run the Gateway installer again there, then restart the Gateway once no tasks are using it. This message often means accessibility components the Gateway needs are missing or broken, and the installer repairs them in place.
  3. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. Existing tasks keep the Gateway abilities they started with; a new task picks up the repaired ones.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows that Gateway as connected, and a new task can read the app's buttons and fields.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the computer's operating system, to the person who manages that Gateway. Repair it in place: don't delete the Gateway's pairing, saved sign-ins, settings or task files. Giving a Skill permission to control apps doesn't install the missing parts.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's native accessibility observation failed, its platform accessibility root was unavailable, or the UI service caught an unclassified error before any input was dispatched.

What this means

  • Native accessibility observation failed or the service caught an unclassified exception before its mutation boundary; readiness can also report that the platform accessibility root is unavailable. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Native accessibility observation failed or the service caught an unclassified exception before its mutation boundary; readiness can also report that the platform accessibility root is unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ui.status and platform root/session readiness, distinguishing missing software from a failed running accessibility service.

How to fix it

  • Run ui.status on the selected Gateway. If PyGObject/AT-SPI (Linux), PyObjC (macOS) or comtypes (Windows) is missing or incompatible, repair the Gateway in place by rerunning its supported installer on that host (Linux: src/gateway_agent/install.sh), then, once active work has settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. If the dependencies are present, restore the interactive desktop and accessibility session and the required OS permissions; start a new task afterwards because existing tasks keep their captured capability snapshot.
  • Inspect ui.status. If PyGObject, AT-SPI, PyObjC or comtypes is missing or incompatible, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. If dependencies are present, restore the interactive desktop/accessibility session and required OS permissions.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended session supplies a valid scoped accessibility snapshot under its existing permissions.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
